response.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT s.healtheval, sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0) AS rate
  FROM scans sc
  JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
),
grp AS (
  SELECT healtheval, AVG(rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS scan_count
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY healtheval
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS overall_rate FROM grp
),
kept AS (
  SELECT g.avg_rate, g.scan_count, o.overall_rate
  FROM grp g
  CROSS JOIN overall o
  WHERE g.avg_rate > o.overall_rate
)
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS avg_rate,
       AVG(scan_count) AS avg_scan_count,
       AVG(avg_rate - overall_rate) AS avg_excess_over_overall
FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: Scans are matched to sites by an inner join, so scans with no matching site are dropped. Rate is gbsize / spanmin per scan, with spanmin = 0 treated as missing (NULLIF) to avoid division by zero. Missing rates are skipped by AVG.
The number of scans per status counts every joined scan in that status, including scans whose rate is missing.
The all-status average rate is the unweighted mean of the per-status average rates, so each status counts equally.
Scans whose site has a NULL healtheval form their own group, as GROUP BY does by default. The request does not say whether they should be excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: The all-status average is the scan-weighted mean of every scan's rate, not the mean of the per-status averages.
